chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Ziyarah (visiting the Kaaba) from Mina. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he visits during the day or in the evening, he must not see the dawn break except while he is in Mina. And if he visits after midnight and approaches dawn, there is no harm if the dawn breaks while he is in Mecca.'
ai.seo_question: When must a pilgrim be in Mina for the dawn prayer after performing Ziyarah from there?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the flexibility of the Mina stay (*Muzdalifah* transition) by linking the validity of the Ziyarah to the specific time of dawn (*Fajr al-Sadiq*). It reflects the Shia juristic view that the ritual requirement is tied to the completion of the night prayer or the specific act of visitation, allowing pilgrims to depart for Mecca if they perform the Ziyarah after midnight, thereby easing the physical burden of the Hajj rites.
